# File Upload Workflow

## File Uploads

File Uploads lets you upload files of any type to customers — documents, images, videos, audio, and more — then notify them with a branded download page.

### Getting Started

File Uploads must be enabled for your organisation and requires S3 storage to be configured. Once enabled, the **File Uploads** option appears in the main navigation sidebar.

Before uploading, configure your **Email Settings** (gear icon) to set your sender name, reply-to address, email subject, body text, and optional logo. You can also set up a **Direct Download Domain** for branded download URLs.

### Uploading Files

Click **Upload Files** to open the uploader. You can:

- **Drop a folder** — the folder name becomes the upload name automatically
- **Select individual files** — you'll be prompted to enter a name for the upload
- **Queue multiple uploads** — add several folders or file batches before starting

Each upload shows a progress bar as files transfer to your S3 storage. You can also assign **Tags** to uploads for organisation and filtering.

### Associating with Orders

After uploading, associate the upload with an order to attach customer details (name, email, order number). This is required before you can send a notification email.

Click the **Link** icon on any upload, then search for and select the matching order. You can also bulk-select multiple uploads and associate them in one step.

### Sending Notifications

Once an upload is associated with an order, you can send the customer an email with a link to their download page. Use the **Send** button on the upload row, or preview the email first to check the content.

The email uses your configured branding — logo, colours, and custom text — and includes a link to the branded download page.

### Download Page

Customers receive a branded download page showing all their files with individual download buttons and a **Download All as ZIP** option. The page displays your organisation's logo, colours, and any custom messages you've configured.

If you've set up **Gallery Order Links**, customers will also see buttons linking to related online galleries for ordering prints or products.

### Creating Galleries

For uploads that contain images, you can create a **Pixfizz Gallery** directly from the upload. Click the gallery icon to generate a customer-facing gallery. Non-image files (PDFs, documents, etc.) are excluded from gallery creation.

### Managing Uploads

The upload list is organised into tabs:

- **Needs Processing** — uploads awaiting association or email sending
- **Sent** — uploads where the notification email has been delivered
- **Archived** — uploads whose S3 files have been deleted (records preserved)
- **All** — every upload regardless of status

Use the **search bar** to filter by folder name, order number, or customer name. Select multiple uploads with checkboxes for bulk actions like delete.

### S3 Sync

If files are uploaded directly to your S3 bucket (outside of OrderHub), click the **Sync from S3** button to detect new folders in the `file-uploads/` prefix. The sync identifies folders that have been stable for at least 5 minutes and creates upload records automatically.

### Storage Management

The storage summary at the top shows your active and archived upload counts and total storage used. **Archiving** an upload deletes the files from S3 but keeps the database record. **Deleting** removes both the files and the record entirely.

### Tags

Tags help categorise and filter uploads. Manage available tags from the organisation settings. When uploading, you can assign one or more tags. Tags appear as badges on each upload row for easy identification.
